text:
bob-customer: Hey team, after our IdP cert rotation this morning users are getting 401s on SSO. Happening only when sign-in is routed through our proxy (https://auth.myshop.example -> https://proxy.example/forward). No errors when hitting IdP directly.

morgan-support: Thanks for the report — can you paste the exact error from the SP logs or a failing request trace? Also which binding (POST/Redirect)?

bob-customer: Error in SP logs: \"SAML assertion rejected: AssertionConsumerService URL mismatch. expected=https://app.myshop.example/saml/acs got=https://proxy.example/forward/saml/acs\" Binding=HTTP-POST. We reproduced in incognito.

morgan-support: That suggests the ACS URL in the incoming assertion doesn't exactly match the SP metadata. Two quick checks: 1) can you share the IdP metadata URL you provided (or paste the <AssertionConsumerService> entry)? 2) did the cert rotation also change any hostnames or proxy prefix rules?

bob-customer: IdP metadata URL: https://idp.cust-idp.example/metadata.xml. I grabbed the ACS entries from the raw assertion (redacted):
```
<AssertionConsumerService Binding=\"urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST\" Location=\"https://app.myshop.example/saml/acs\"/>
```
But our proxy rewrites host/path so the request reaching the SP looks like Location https://proxy.example/forward/saml/acs (we think).

kevin-identity: @bob-customer thanks. Two probable problems: (A) proxy rewrites are changing the Host/Request-URI and SP is validating the assertion Recipient/ACS against observed URL, so mismatch. (B) IdP may have been configured with the SP's pre-proxy public ACS but the proxy fronting the app changes what SP sees. Did the proxy add an X-Forwarded-Host or X-Forwarded-Proto header?

bob-customer: Proxy does set X-Forwarded-* headers and preserves TLS to backend. We verified with a curl to backend and see Host: proxy.example and X-Forwarded-Host: app.myshop.example. SP still logs the observed request URL as https://proxy.example/forward/saml/acs

morgan-support: If SP uses the actual request Host for ACS validation, you have to ensure either: 1) SP sees the original host (unrewrite Host header), or 2) IdP metadata contains the proxy URL as an allowed ACS. Quick workaround: add the proxy-facing ACS URL to your SP metadata and re-publish to IdP (or configure your SP to respect X-Forwarded-Host when validating ACS).

kevin-identity: Also confirm the Recipient attribute in the assertion (if present) exactly matches ACS Location. Some libraries compare Recipient, AssertionConsumerServiceIndex, and the Location value. If the IdP signed-metadata changed during rotation, check that the signed metadata you fetched is the latest one (fingerprint of cert). run: 
```
curl -sSf https://idp.cust-idp.example/metadata.xml | xmllint --format - | sed -n '1,120p'
```
and check <KeyDescriptor use=\"signing\"> cert and <AssertionConsumerService> entries.

deploy-bot: [deploy-notice] idp.cust-idp.example cert rotation completed at 2025-06-12T09:05:12Z by ops-team.

bob-customer: We re-fetched metadata and it shows same ACS as before (https://app.myshop.example/saml/acs). The cert fingerprint changed per deploy-bot. The IdP team says they only rotated certs, not metadata hostnames.

jules-engineer: If cert rotated, but your proxy rewrites Host, then assertion signature validation will still succeed (cert unrelated to Host), but ACS mismatch is independent. Two paths: (1) have SP canonicalize request URL using X-Forwarded headers before comparing to assertion Recipient — patch in SP config; (2) ask IdP to include the proxy-facing ACS as an additional AssertionConsumerService entry so Recipient/Location match; (3) configure the SP metadata to include both hostnames and publish to IdP.

morgan-support: Can you share the SP library and version? Some SAML toolkits expose a setting like preserve_url_scheme or use_x_forwarded_host. If you're on python3-saml or passport-saml, there are options.

bob-customer: We're on auth-service v2.1.3 (java-saml toolkit). No explicit x-forwarded option in our config.

kevin-identity: For java-saml there is an option to set the AssertionConsumerService URL explicitly in the SP config (instead of deriving from request). Set it to your proxy-visible URL or the canonical app URL and ensure IdP metadata includes that same string. Example config snippet: 
```
sp.setAssertionConsumerServiceUrl("https://proxy.example/forward/saml/acs");
```
But that's only viable if IdP accepts the change.

bob-customer: Quick test: we added the proxy ACS to our local SP metadata (manually) and pushed that to a staging IdP binding. After that staging sign-ins worked. So it does look like ACS mismatch.

morgan-support: Great repro, that narrows it. For production: either update the IdP metadata with the extra ACS entry, or change proxy behavior to preserve the original Host header through to backend so the SP sees app.myshop.example. Pros/cons: updating IdP requires coordination with IdP admin; preserving host in proxy might be faster but could affect routing rules.

kevin-identity: Also double-check for trailing slash, port, and presence of path prefix. The logs showed "/forward/saml/acs" vs "/saml/acs" — those need to match exactly.

bob-customer: Understood. We'll coordinate with IdP to add the proxy-facing ACS entry and also evaluate a proxy config tweak. Will report back. Thanks! :pray:

morgan-support: Thanks for the quick repro and test. Please ping here once IdP is updated; if anything still fails include a signed assertion (redacted) and the exact SP log lines.

bob-customer: Update: IdP admin added the proxy-facing ACS entry and rotated metadata (new metadata fetched). We still saw a 401 for mobile SSO flows. Turned out mobile uses a different redirect prefix (/m/forward/saml/acs). We added that variant to SP metadata too and mobile started working.

jules-engineer: Nice catch. Glad it was just ACS normalization/variants. If you want, we can open a small PR on auth-service to add a config option to accept a list of allowed ACS aliases and to prefer X-Forwarded-Host when present. Will make future rotations less painful.

bob-customer: That would be awesome. For now :thumbsup: all green. Closing the incident on our side.

morgan-support: Marking resolved on support side. Thanks for the collaboration! :white_check_mark:
